title: Telehealth policy brief with unrelated recruiting update
instruction: Produce a policy memo recommending whether a multistate health system should expand telehealth service lines for follow-up behavioral-health and chronic-care visits over the next 24 months. The memo must synthesize current evidence, preserve unresolved tensions, and avoid using adjacent but decision-irrelevant materials.

workflow_stages.label: Utilization Context
workflow_stages.purpose: Summarize current utilization and adoption evidence.

workflow_stages.label: Reimbursement Context
workflow_stages.purpose: Summarize current reimbursement and parity evidence.

workflow_stages.label: Operations Context
workflow_stages.purpose: Summarize current compliance, workflow, and adoption constraints.

workflow_stages.label: Access vs Cost Context
workflow_stages.purpose: Summarize access benefits, continuity gains, and cost uncertainty.

workflow_stages.label: Provider Recruiting Note
workflow_stages.purpose: Summarize the separate provider recruiting and staffing branch.

workflow_stages.label: Claim Matrix
workflow_stages.purpose: Map candidate claims to current supporting sources and mark stale or excluded claims.

workflow_stages.label: Recommendation Criteria
workflow_stages.purpose: Define recommendation criteria grounded in current claims and tensions.

workflow_stages.label: Final Memo
workflow_stages.purpose: Write the final memo using only the declared telehealth decision artifacts.

update_user_note: One of the supporting materials was updated. Revise the memo only if the current evidence changes the telehealth service-line recommendation.

claim_matrix_current: Expand behavioral-health follow-up more confidently than chronic-care follow-up.
Do not claim universal parity or system-wide savings.
Use payer validation, state-cluster compliance readiness, and utilization controls as rollout gates.
tension_analysis_current: Access gains and continuity benefits can coexist with utilization growth and cost uncertainty.
The recommendation should stay focused on telehealth evidence, not adjacent staffing strategy.
